errors.problem: سَيَخْرُجُ is 3rd person singular; '(they)' is the subject of one sentence (verb before a plural noun), not the meaning of the word
errors.fix: (he) will go out, will leave

errors.problem: سَيَأْتِي is singular (he/it will come); '(they)' is sentence-specific
errors.fix: and (he, it) will come

errors.problem: the gloss gives the plural subject of one sentence and leaks a grammar note; يَصُومُ means 'he fasts'
errors.fix: (he) fasts (singular form, also used before a plural subject)

errors.current: عنها = about them (lit. about it, f)
errors.problem: عَنْهَا = about her / about it (f); 'about them' is only true for a non-human plural antecedent in one sentence, and a beginner will learn -hā = them
errors.fix: about her, about it (f) (also 'about them' when it refers to a non-human plural)

errors.current: قالها = (they) said them (lit. he said it); يقرؤها = (they) read them (lit. he reads it)
errors.problem: subject and object are both taken from one sentence; the word itself is singular subject + feminine singular object
errors.fix: قالها = (he) said it (f) (or 'said them': non-human plural); يقرؤها = (he) reads it (f) (or 'reads them': non-human plural)

errors.problem: the unvocalised key also covers عُمَان = Oman (the country); both occur in a Middle-East course and a learner tapping عُمَان gets 'Amman'
errors.fix: Amman (ʿAmmān, capital of Jordan); Oman (ʿUmān, the country)

errors.problem: ظُهْرًا = 'at noon' is the far more common reading of this spelling (ẕuhran, time adverb); ظَهْرًا = 'a back' (object form) is the other
errors.fix: at noon (ẕuhran); a back (ẕahran, object form)

errors.problem: يَعْلَمُ = he knows (Form I) is the basic and most frequent reading; يُعَلِّمُ = he teaches (Form II). The gloss gives only the Form II sense
errors.fix: (he) knows (yaʿlamu); (he) teaches (yuʿallimu)

errors.problem: عَلِمْتُ = I knew / I found out (Form I) shares the spelling, as do عَلَّمْتَ 'you taught' and عَلِمَتْ 'she knew'; one-sided
errors.fix: I knew, I found out (ʿalimtu); I taught (ʿallamtu); also you (m/f) / she with the same spelling

errors.current: عرفنا = introduce to us! (to a man)
errors.problem: عَرَفْنَا = we knew / we got to know is the plain Form I reading; the gloss gives only the Form II imperative عَرِّفْنَا from one dialogue
errors.fix: we knew, we got to know (ʿarafnā); introduce to us! (ʿarrifnā, to a man)

errors.problem: عَبْرَ = through, across (preposition) and عَبَرَ = he crossed are the common readings; the gloss gives only the Form II imperative عَبِّرْ
errors.fix: through, across (ʿabra); (he) crossed (ʿabara); express! (ʿabbir, to a man)

errors.problem: the active صَنَعَ 'he made' shares the spelling with the passive صُنِعَ; a beginner reading صَنَعَ gets a passive
errors.fix: (he) made (ṣanaʿa); (it) was made (ṣuniʿa); making (ṣunʿ)

errors.problem: قُلْتُ 'I said' is the most frequent reading of this spelling; قُلْتَ 'you said (m)' also shares it. Giving only the feminine 2nd person is wrong almost everywhere else
errors.fix: I said (qultu); you said (qulta to a man, qulti to a woman)

errors.current: نجحت = you succeeded ('will pass', to a man)
errors.problem: one person only (نَجَحْتُ 'I passed' and نَجَحَتْ 'she passed' share the spelling) and a future tense from one sentence leaked into a past-tense word
errors.fix: you passed, succeeded (to a man); I passed (najaḥtu); she passed (najaḥat)

errors.problem: وُلِدَ = (he) was born shares the spelling and is very common in biographies and 'I was born in…' sentences
errors.fix: boy (walad); (he) was born (wulida)

errors.problem: وَجَدْتُهُ = I found him / I found it is the basic verb reading of this spelling; the gloss gives only wa- + jaddatuhu
errors.fix: I found him, I found it (wajadtuhu); and his grandmother (wa-jaddatuhu)

errors.problem: وَجَدَّتُهَا = and her grandmother shares the spelling (the course uses جدة often); also 'I found her'
errors.fix: I found it (f), I found her (wajadtuhā); and her grandmother (wa-jaddatuhā)

errors.path: شربت; صححت; غسلت; فقدت; قدمت; لبست; مشيت; نسيت; نظفت; نظمت; غبت; ظننت; فزت; قضيت; لاحظت; وجدت; وأخذت; وتركت; وسألت; ودفعت; ونسيت; وشربت; وشعرت; وسمعت; وفهمت; وكتبت; ونمت; وبقيت; واشتريت; واشترت; وقالت; وطبخت; فكتبت; فتكلمت; فأجبت; فسألته; صنعته; نسيتها; شاهدتك; علمتنا; غادرت; ضاعت
errors.problem: systematic: every past-tense verb ending in -ت is glossed with the one person of the sentence it came from (I / you (m) / you (f) / she), but the unvocalised spelling covers شَرِبْتُ I, شَرِبْتَ you (m), شَرِبْتِ you (f) and شَرِبَتْ she. A learner tapping وَأَخَذْتُ 'and I took' reads 'and she took'; tapping فَسَأَلْتُهُ 'so I asked him' reads 'so she asked him'
errors.fix: add the persons that share the spelling, in the pattern 'I drank; you drank (m/f); she drank' (for the object forms: 'I / you / she … him/it'); e.g. شربت = I drank; you drank (m/f); she drank (sharibat)

errors.path: طلبك; عنوانك; واسمك; ولصديقك; يدك; نساعدك; نعطيك
errors.problem: the suffix -ك is gender-neutral without harakat (-ka / -ki); these seven entries take '(to a woman)' from one sentence while the rest of the file says '(to a man)'; both are sentence-specific
errors.fix: your application, your request (to one person: -ka to a man, -ki to a woman); same pattern for the other six (your address; and your name; and for your friend; your hand; we help you; we give you)

errors.problem: the spelling also covers فَهُمْ = 'so they, and they' (fa- + hum), a very frequent word in connected text, and the noun فَهْم 'understanding'
errors.fix: (he) understood (fahima); understanding (fahm); so they (fa-hum)

errors.current: مذكرة = masculine (agreeing with a feminine noun)
errors.problem: confusing wording (reads as a contradiction) and misses مُذَكِّرَة = notebook, memo, which shares the spelling
errors.fix: masculine (f form of the adjective, e.g. 'the word is masculine'); a notebook, a memo (mudhakkira)

errors.problem: تَأْمِين means insurance; 'deposit' is only the security-deposit sense of one rental dialogue
errors.fix: and the insurance; and the (security) deposit

errors.problem: الكِبَار as a group of people means the adults, the grown-ups (vs الصغار the children), not the elderly
errors.fix: and the adults, the grown-ups

errors.problem: وَزْن primarily means weight; 'pattern' is only the grammar-lesson sense
errors.fix: and the weight; and the (word) pattern (grammar)

errors.problem: وَصْفَة also means recipe (cooking), a sense a food-heavy course will hit
errors.fix: prescription; recipe

errors.problem: وَقَّعَ = he signed (contracts, forms) shares the spelling
errors.fix: (it) fell (waqaʿa); (he) signed (waqqaʿa)

errors.problem: وَبُنِّيّ = and brown (colour) shares the spelling; colours are taught in the course
errors.fix: and (it) was built (wa-buniya); and brown (wa-bunnī)

errors.problem: وَفُرْنًا / وَفُرْنُنَا = and an oven / and our oven shares the spelling (فرن is in the glossary)
errors.fix: we saved (waffarnā); and an oven (wa-furnan)

errors.problem: كَرِيم is also the ordinary adjective generous, kind (the feminine كريمة is glossed 'generous (f)' two lines below)
errors.fix: generous, kind; Karim (first name)

errors.problem: عَامّ = general, public shares the spelling (e.g. مكان عام, رأي عام)
errors.fix: year (ʿām); general, public (ʿāmm)

errors.problem: noun + possessive and verb + pronoun share the spelling: كَتَبَهَا he wrote it / كُتُبُهَا her books, كَتَبَهُ / كُتُبُهُ, كَتَبْنَا / كُتُبُنَا, عَمِلْنَا / عَمَلُنَا, طَلَبْنَا / طَلَبُنَا; each entry gives one side only
errors.fix: كتبها = her books; (he) wrote it (f) · كتبه = (he) wrote it; his books · كتبنا = we wrote; our books · عملنا = we worked; our work · طلبنا = we asked for; our request, our order

errors.problem: شُرْب = drinking (verbal noun) shares the spelling and appears in phrases like ماء الشرب
errors.fix: (he) drank (shariba); drinking (shurb)

errors.current: شغل = play, switch on (to a man)
errors.problem: شُغْل = work, a job is the common noun with this spelling; the gloss gives only the Form II imperative شَغِّلْ
errors.fix: work, a job (shughl); switch on, play! (shaghghil, to a man)

errors.problem: فَخِذ = thigh shares the spelling (body-part lessons)
errors.fix: then take! (fa-khudh, to a man); thigh (fakhidh)

errors.current: غطيت = (they) were covered (-i links to the next word)
errors.problem: an engine/editorial note has leaked into the gloss, the subject '(they)' is sentence-specific (غُطِّيَتْ is 'it (f) was covered'), and غَطَّيْتُ 'I covered' shares the spelling
errors.fix: (it, f) was covered (ghuṭṭiyat; also for a non-human plural); I covered (ghaṭṭaytu)

errors.problem: 'to back' is not an English gloss; لِظَهْر = for the back (of), and لِظُهْر = for noon shares the spelling
errors.fix: for the back (of) (li-ẕahr); for noon (li-ẕuhr)

errors.problem: 'medium sweet' is the coffee-order sense of one dialogue; the word means exact, correct, just right everywhere else
errors.fix: exact, correct, just right (of coffee: medium sweet)

errors.current: وأقدم = and the oldest (before a noun)
errors.problem: وَأُقَدِّمُ = and I present / I introduce shares the spelling (the course glosses سيقدم and قدمت as 'present')
errors.fix: and the oldest, older (wa-aqdam, before a noun); and I present, I introduce (wa-uqaddimu)

errors.problem: مُوَافَقَة = approval, consent (noun) shares the spelling and is common in forms and official texts
errors.fix: agreed, OK (said by a woman); approval, consent (noun)

errors.problem: verb and wa-+noun share these spellings: وَجَدْتِ you (f) found / وَجَدَّتِي and my grandmother; وَجَدْنَا we found / وَجَدُّنَا and our grandfather
errors.fix: وجدتي = and my grandmother (wa-jaddatī); you found (wajadti, to a woman) · وجدنا = we found (wajadnā); and our grandfather (wa-jaddunā)

notes.note: About 60 entries with -ك / -ك- are labelled '(to a man)'. The unvocalised key cannot tell -ka from -ki, so the label is a convention rather than a fact; consider '(to one person)' or 'your (m/f)' as the house pattern so that the seven '(to a woman)' entries do not look like a different rule.
English agreement slips in the gloss: 'he see', '(he) fail', '(he) feel', '(he) interrupt', '(it) appear' should read 'he sees', 'fails', 'feels', 'interrupts', 'appears'. Not an Arabic error.
'piasters (1/100 of a dinar)': the qirsh is 1/100 of a Jordanian dinar but also 1/100 of an Egyptian pound; if the sentence is set in Egypt the parenthesis is wrong. Check the source sentence.
'their point (post)' is unclear English: if the sentence means a checkpoint or a (score) point, say so.

notes.note: Quoted sentence renderings such as ('will pass'), ('can we find'), ('should we bring'), ('forget'), ('we work'), ('correct') give a tense or mood that is not in the word. They are marked with quotes so a careful reader sees they are contextual; consider dropping them in the auto glossary.

summary: Read all ~1,700 entries of audit/glossary-auto-2.txt (س–ي) as dictionary glosses for unvocalised keys. 40 findings: 17 major, 23 minor. The main patterns: (1) person taken from one sentence rather than from the word: singular verbs glossed '(they)' (سيخرج, وسيأتي, يصوم), -hā glossed 'them' (عنها, قالها, يقرؤها), and a systematic one-person gloss on every past-tense -ت verb (شربت = 'I drank' only, قلت = 'you said (to a woman)' only, وأخذت = 'she took' only) across more than 40 keys; (2) one-sided glosses where the spelling covers two common words: عمان Amman/Oman, ظهرا back/at noon, يعلم teaches/knows, علمت taught/knew, عرفنا introduce!/we knew, عبر express!/through, صنع was made/made, ولد boy/was born, وجدته and his grandmother/I found it, عام, كريم, وقع, وصفة, والتأمين, والوزن, والكبار; (3) small leaks of sentence context or engine notes into the gloss (غطيت '-i links to the next word', نجحت 'will pass', مضبوط 'medium sweet', يصوم 'verb first: singular'); (4) the -ك gender label '(to a man)' vs '(to a woman)' is a convention that the key cannot support (minor, 7 inconsistent entries). The and-/for-/the- compound entries (و-, ل-, لل-, وال-), numbers, food, names, months and most adjectives were checked and are correct.
